_comment: Your standing weekly availability. 'all-day' or 'off'. The web UI does not read this file, only the CLI does.
_weeklyHourCap: Warn when a week goes over this many hours. null disables it. On-campus student jobs are often capped at 20 during term.
_pay: Remove this block to hide the pay panel. nightFrom/nightTo are start hours, so 0-6 means a shift starting at midnight bills at the night rate. taxRate is your own effective withholding, taken off a real payslip, not a guess.
_madmax: The armed auto-claimer. checkOnly asks the server whether a shift is claimable and logs the answer WITHOUT taking it, which is how to prove the claim path safely; set it false to claim for real. intervalSeconds is a backstop, not the detector: detection lives on the counts lane below, so this only exists to catch a posting the counts lane missed, and every tick of it spends board allowance that an aimed read would rather have. 60/intervalSeconds must stay under budget.routinePerMinute or the extra ticks are simply held. stationWeights biases the optimiser: 1.2 makes an hour at that post worth 1.2 of an hour elsewhere, and it maximises total hours when left empty.

madmax._budget: How much the swapboard endpoint may be asked, ever, by anything. See budget.mjs. routinePerMinute is what clock ticks may spend; the gap up to perMinute is reserved for reads that the counts detector, a mail trigger or a manual refresh asked for, so an empty board cannot spend the allowance the one interesting moment needs. These defaults are slower than the 5s sweep that earned a 30 minute lockout on 2026-08-21. Raise them only against measured numbers from probe.mjs, never on a hunch.
madmax._detect: The fast lane. swapboardCounts covers ~84 days in one request and is not spacing-limited (measured: 4 calls at every gap down to 200ms, no refusal), so detection lives there and the rate-limited board endpoint is only read once a count actually moves. detectIntervalSeconds is bounded by countsBudget, not by the endpoint: 24/min is what probe.mjs has demonstrated without a refusal, while 60/min was refused outright on 2026-08-21. Run probe.mjs --run --sustain=counts to find the real ceiling before lowering this.

_mail: Push instead of polling, and the only thing that can catch a shift that lives for a second. IMAP IDLE wakes the claimer the moment your mail server accepts a TeamWork notification, and it costs zero swapboard requests so it cannot trip the rate limit. Set host/user for wherever the notifications land (imap.gmail.com, or outlook.office365.com for a university account) and store the password the same way as the TeamWork one: security add-generic-password -s tmwork-rso -a YOUR_EMAIL -w. Gmail needs an app password, not your login password. Leave triggerSubject empty until you have seen the real subject line, because empty means every TeamWork mail triggers a look, which is the safe default. Delete this block to run on polling alone.
_maps: Station names are turned into Google Maps searches. campus is appended to sharpen the search. Put an override in stations only when Google resolves a name badly, e.g. "INV Northwest 1": "42.3406,-71.0890".
